subject: Competitive econ heatcheck + next tests
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Maya Ramey <maya@kiln.so>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Competitive econ heatcheck + next tests

Hi Maya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the comparison plan and what data will make the tests decisive.

Recap (from our side):
- Hyperscaler claims you quoted: ~ $16 / 1M tokens for text-generation (p50 latency 150–200ms) when using their managed endpoint with z-series GPUs and 8-token batching.
- Kiln mentioned production profile: 60% short prompts (<64 tokens), 30% mid (64–512), 10% long (>512); expected steady-state ~400 qps peak.
- Key switchpoints we need to validate: batching impact across your prompt distribution, effective KV/prefix cache hit rate impact on token cost, and network egress/ingress cost for private data.

What we propose to run as next tests: (minimal, low-friction)
1) 100k token smoke against your representative sample (we'll run in our hosted environment) with three configs:
   - low batch (b=1),
   - mid batch (b=8),
   - high batch (b=32)
   Objective: measure per-1M token runtime cost, p50/p95 latency, and GPU utilization.
2) Cache hit emulation: we will replay a 48-hour prefix trace to estimate KV cache hit ratio; we will surface effective token savings and latency delta.
3) End-to-end TCO sketch: we will produce a 12-month, 1M/10M/100M token bucket comparison vs the hyperscaler including egress and reserved capacity assumptions.

Attachments: redwood-econ-sheet-v1.xlsx (simple template for the test outputs) and a short diagram showing routing assumptions (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-diagram.png).

Asks from Kiln: please share (1) a 10–20k token sample that reflects your traffic mix (paste link or upload), (2) any constraints around IP/ingress (do we need a signed NDA for test data?), and (3) preferred date windows for running a 2-hour test window next week.

I copied Ben and Karthik to keep the benchmarks reproducible and to capture billing/ops constraints. If that sounds good, we can lock a slot — Ben, can you propose two 2-hour windows Wed/Thu next week?

Thanks,
Laura

Subject: Re: Competitive econ heatcheck + next tests

Thanks Laura — appreciate the structured plan. A few clarifications from our side before we surface the sample: 

- The hyperscaler number you quoted is in the ballpark of what we saw, but that included a reserved instance discount and assumed egress within their cloud. We have non-trivial egress to our analytics cluster. Can you explicitly include a line item for egress in the TCO?

- We can share the sample trace, but we need a standard NDA before uploading anything PII-adjacent. Procurement looped in.

- For scheduling, Thu morning PT works better for our ops team (08:00–10:00 PT). Would that be possible?

One ask: can you also provide a short note on how Redwood handles quantized model accuracy vs hyperscaler-managed FP16 endpoints? We want to see likely quality delta if you recommend int8/4-bit quantization for cost savings.

-Maya
Maya Ramey
Head of ML Ops, Kiln Software
maya@kiln.so

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Competitive econ heatcheck + next tests

Hi Maya — quick answers and a more detailed test plan attached.

Egress: we'll include a line in the TCO with two scenarios: (A) egress to same cloud region (low), (B) egress to external analytics cluster (higher) — both with bandwidth cost assumptions.

Quantization and accuracy: short answer — quantization (int8 / 4-bit) reduces serving cost significantly and, for many instruction-following tasks, quality impact is minimal if you use post-training calibration and Redwood's per-model quantization profile. We'll include a small accuracy checklist and the quantization profile we propose for your model family in the attached workbook. Important call-outs:
- For classification or high-stakes generation, we recommend controlled A/B tests (sample of recent prompts).
- For short prompts (your 60%), quantization shows >2.5x cost improvement at <3% ROUGE-style quality delta in our internal evals; for long contexts (>512) the delta can be larger depending on attention math.

Proposed concrete test steps (attached as sheet + runbook):
1) Confirm NDA — procurement to confirm by EOD tomorrow.
2) Slot for performance run: Thu 08:00–10:00 PT (we tentatively reserve).
3) We will run 3 workload configs and produce a 6-page TCO summary within 48 hours of test completion.
4) If quantization A/B looks promising, follow-up regression evals against a 5k prompt set.

Attachments included: redwood-econ-sheet-v1.xlsx (filled test plan tab), redwood-quant-profiles.pdf (note: referenced in the spreadsheet).

Ben Carter

Confirmed actions and owners: 
- Procurement (Kiln): provide NDA or confirmation by 2026-08-26 EOD.
- Kiln ML: upload 10–20k token representative sample to the Drive link once NDA done.
- Redwood (Ben): run the 2-hour perf window on Thu 2026-08-27 08:00–10:00 PT, capture p50/p95 latency, GPU utilization, batch size delta, and effective token accounting given simulated cache hits. Produce the 6-page TCO within 48 hours.
- Redwood (Laura): provide a short plain-English summary of the quantization tradeoffs and an initial per-1M token TCO estimate by test completion.

If anything changes on timing, flag here. Otherwise we'll proceed as above. Looking forward to the results — our goal is to give Kiln a transparent, apples-to-apples TCO so you can make a confident decision between the hyperscaler and Redwood's Dedicated/Private options.

Thanks,
Laura
